adrs.name: Version-controlled project truth and machine-local runtime truth
Loopback API and closed permission model
Execution profiles separate from instructions and Skills
Checkout-local daemon is the only CLI execution worker
Instruction-directed project context and sortable ordering
Action-specific Codex Agents are execution instruction truth

constraints.description: Human decisions and deterministic State and Action gates remain authoritative.
constraints.name: Human approval and ordered execution integrity
constraints.rationale: The runtime must preserve operator authority and explain every progression decision.

constraints.description: An Action reads relevant Goals, ADRs, Constraints and Use Cases only when its selected instruction or Skill requires them.
constraints.name: Read required project direction
constraints.rationale: Project context stays explicit without a platform-owned closure.

constraints.description: Every Action runs the checks named by its instruction and reports their exact outcome.
constraints.name: Run exact validation
constraints.rationale: Completion must be reproducible from concrete checks.

constraints.description: Changes preserve explicit domain boundaries, single ownership and maintainable dependencies.
constraints.name: Preserve clean architecture
constraints.rationale: A local success must not create hidden coupling or duplicate truth.

constraints.description: Validation may return done only with stable, independently inspectable evidence.
constraints.name: Evidence is required for done
constraints.rationale: Provider prose is not an execution fact.

constraints.description: Repository writes stay within the managed worktree and approved path boundary.
constraints.name: Use safe paths and isolated worktrees
constraints.rationale: The active checkout and unrelated files must remain protected.

constraints.description: Core workflows remain keyboard-operable, labelled and usable at the accepted desktop and narrow viewports.
constraints.name: Meet accessibility and responsive contracts
constraints.rationale: Operator authority must not depend on pointer input, color or a wide screen.

constraints.description: No later State or lower-priority bypass may start before every preceding gate is done.
constraints.name: No premature State progression
constraints.rationale: Deterministic order is the Environment control contract.

constraints.description: Agents cannot approve Use Cases, Critic proposals or Refinement proposals.
constraints.name: No agent self-approval
constraints.rationale: Proposal authority and human decision authority must stay separate.

constraints.description: Local execution never merges, pushes, publishes or deploys without a separate exact human authorization.
constraints.name: No automatic merge push release or deploy
constraints.rationale: A local run does not grant external lifecycle authority.

constraints.description: Agents do not write to external services without explicit scoped human authorization.
constraints.name: No unauthorized external writes
constraints.rationale: Execution profiles and prompts cannot widen external authority.

constraints.description: The strict target does not add migrations, compatibility readers, route aliases or dual writes.
constraints.name: No compatibility or dual-write paths
constraints.rationale: One canonical contract keeps the pre-production system understandable and fail-closed.

constraints.description: Ballet-specific workflow identifiers and procedures do not appear in generic backend, frontend or shared platform logic.
constraints.name: No project workflow in platform code
constraints.rationale: The platform must execute arbitrary project-local Environments.

constraints.description: Checks are not fabricated, disabled or skipped to claim completion.
constraints.name: No fake validation or skipped failures
constraints.rationale: Failing evidence must remain visible and actionable.

constraints.description: Secrets, credentials and unredacted sensitive values never enter prompts, events or retained logs.
constraints.name: No secrets in prompts or logs
constraints.rationale: Immutable evidence must be safe to inspect.

examples.given: the project needs a bounded outcome
examples.then: the project records one explicit version-controlled decision context
examples.when: the human maintains Goals, ADRs and Constraints

expectedOutcomes: Traceable project-local Direction available through explicit instruction or Skill guidance
failureGoals: No provider prompt becomes an alternative source of project intent
useCases.name: Define project direction

examples.given: a draft Use Case with acceptance intent
examples.then: the approval becomes project evidence without binding Environment execution
examples.when: the human approves its exact semantic hash

examples.given: an approved Use Case
examples.then: approval is invalidated without blocking unrelated Environment runs

expectedOutcomes: An immutable approval record bound to one canonical content hash
failureGoals: No stale approval survives a semantic edit
useCases.name: Describe and approve a Use Case
successGoals: Exact human-approved Use Cases remain trustworthy project evidence

examples.given: an Action traces to accepted architecture
examples.then: the role reads the relevant canonical .ballet documents
examples.when: its selected instruction or Skill requires project direction

expectedOutcomes: A hash-bound instruction and Skill closure with explicit document-reading guidance
failureGoals: No Action relies on ambient or obsolete architecture context
useCases.name: Provide architecture decisions to agents
successGoals: Architecture decisions reach every affected Action

examples.given: approved work with multiple dependency stages
examples.then: the Environment exposes one deterministic progression path

examples.given: duplicate or empty State ordering
examples.then: the Environment is rejected before provider dispatch

expectedOutcomes: A strict Environment definition with unique ascending State order
failureGoals: No freeform topology or ambiguous State order is runnable
useCases.name: Model work as an Environment
successGoals: Work is decomposed into ordered and inspectable States

examples.given: a State with multiple Actions
examples.then: it dispatches the lowest-priority-number pending Action

examples.given: an earlier Action or State is not done
examples.then: zero later Actions are dispatched

expectedOutcomes: Ascending priority execution inside the first incomplete State
failureGoals: No pending or blocked predecessor can be bypassed
useCases.name: Process State Actions by priority
successGoals: Action selection is deterministic and gate-safe

examples.given: one bounded capability is needed
examples.then: Validation and Work receive an executable immutable composition
examples.when: the human defines its task, evidence, retries, roles and resources

expectedOutcomes: An Action with exact instructions, Skills and retry limit
failureGoals: No single Action represents the whole project
useCases.name: Define an Action
successGoals: Every Action is bounded, resourced and independently verifiable

examples.given: a pending Action
examples.then: it returns only done, delegate or blocked with evidence

examples.given: insufficient or contradictory evidence
examples.then: it cannot return done

failureGoals: No false done or Work-first execution
useCases.name: Check Action readiness
successGoals: Validation proves completion or bounds the next work before any write

examples.given: Validation returns delegate with a bounded dynamic prompt
examples.then: Work executes only that prompt in the managed worktree

examples.given: Work attempts an approval or external write
examples.then: the operation is denied

expectedOutcomes: A completed or needs-input Work outcome for Validation to postcheck
failureGoals: Work cannot route, approve or widen its permissions
useCases.name: Delegate bounded work to a subordinate agent
successGoals: Subordinate Work is isolated and explicitly scoped

examples.given: Validation rejects completed Work while retry budget remains
examples.then: one additional Work attempt receives the correction

examples.given: the final allowed Work attempt still needs retry
examples.then: the Action and exactly one Feedback entry are committed atomically as blocked

expectedOutcomes: Done, a bounded retry, or atomic blocked Feedback
failureGoals: No provider failure silently consumes semantic retry budget
useCases.name: Retry or block an Action
successGoals: Semantic retries are bounded and blockers stay visible

examples.given: every Environment Action is done and finalization succeeds
examples.then: a Run Evidence projects commit, artifacts, statuses, approvals and evidence

examples.given: the Environment is incomplete or blocked
examples.then: no terminal Run Evidence is invented

expectedOutcomes: A recomputable terminal projection linked to canonical truth
failureGoals: No provider prose or partial run becomes a Run Evidence
useCases.name: Form the final Run Evidence
successGoals: The final evidence is factual, immutable and inspectable

examples.given: a disabled default Critic schedule
examples.then: no automatic provider run starts

examples.given: an enabled due occurrence with a valid lease
examples.then: it produces at most one read-only proposal and no Feedback
examples.when: Critic inspects the latest Run Evidence

expectedOutcomes: An immutable Critic proposal awaiting a human decision
failureGoals: No schedule overlap, write or autonomous approval
useCases.name: Run scheduled quality criticism
successGoals: Quality criticism is scheduled, non-overlapping and evidence-based

examples.given: a Critic proposal with exact revision and hash
examples.then: exactly one provenance-bound Feedback entry is appended

examples.given: a rejected, stale or unapproved proposal
examples.then: it contributes zero Feedback entries

expectedOutcomes: Append-only Feedback with exact proposal provenance
failureGoals: No proposal is treated as Feedback before approval
useCases.name: Approve and collect Feedback
successGoals: Only deliberate human-approved criticism enters the Feedback Box

examples.given: approved Feedback and a read-only exact-hash Refinement proposal
examples.then: one managed-worktree commit creates one immutable continuation run
examples.when: the human approves the exact impact and apply succeeds

examples.given: a stale preimage, forbidden path or incomplete shared Skill impact
examples.then: zero project files and zero continuation runs are created

expectedOutcomes: A verified refinement commit and lineage-bound continuation run
failureGoals: No proposal writes, partial apply or parent-run mutation
useCases.name: Refine an Action and rerun immutably
successGoals: Approved refinement is exact, local and auditable

environment.description: Deliver a bounded change through Event Storming, arc42 architecture, Penpot-assisted design, test-driven implementation and the deployment plan defined by arc42.
environment.name: Ballet development lifecycle

actions.description: Maintain the bounded system purpose, stakeholders, essential requirements and measurable quality goals.

acceptance: Purpose, stakeholders, requirements and quality goals are evidence-backed

actions.name: Arc42 - Introduction & Goals

actions.description: Maintain regulatory, organizational, technical and project constraints as explicit facts or accepted decisions.

acceptance: Every active constraint has an owner, rationale and factual status

actions.name: Arc42 - Constraints

actions.description: Maintain system boundaries, external actors, neighboring systems and inbound and outbound interfaces.

acceptance: Every external interface has a named actor, direction and responsibility boundary

actions.name: Arc42 - Context & Scope

actions.description: Maintain the core solution ideas that satisfy the accepted goals, constraints and quality drivers.

acceptance: Every strategy choice traces to an accepted driver and names rejected alternatives where significant

actions.name: Arc42 - Solution Strategy

actions.description: Maintain the static decomposition, responsibilities, interfaces, source mappings and quality significance of important building blocks.

acceptance: Each important block has one responsibility, explicit interfaces and a source owner

actions.name: Arc42 - Building Block View

actions.description: Maintain architecturally significant runtime scenarios, interactions, control ownership and failure behavior.

acceptance: Each retained runtime scenario is risk- or quality-significant and consistent with building blocks

actions.name: Arc42 - Runtime View

actions.description: Define the environment-derived deployment topology, exact dev deployment procedure, health checks and rollback boundary without hardcoding a target in the workflow.

acceptance: The deployment plan names the target, commands, version identity, health criteria and rollback before Deploy can run

actions.name: Arc42 - Deployment View

actions.description: Maintain crosscutting domain, persistence, security, validation, observability and delivery concepts in their smallest canonical location.

acceptance: Recurring concepts have one owner and remain consistent across views and decisions

actions.name: Arc42 - Crosscutting Concepts

actions.description: Maintain the index of important accepted, proposed and superseded architecture decisions without changing accepted semantics silently.

acceptance: Every architecture-significant choice has an explicit status, drivers, consequences and review trigger

actions.name: Arc42 - Architectural Decisions

actions.description: Maintain measurable quality scenarios and their executable or explicitly pending evidence links.

acceptance: Priority scenarios have observable stimuli, exact pass criteria and truthful evidence status

actions.name: Arc42 - Quality Requirements

actions.description: Maintain evidence-backed architecture risks, technical debt, mitigations and unresolved decision pressure.

acceptance: Each active risk names impact, likelihood, affected IDs, mitigation and evidence status

actions.name: Arc42 - Risks & Technical Debt

actions.description: Maintain one unambiguous ubiquitous language shared by Event Storming, architecture, design, tests and implementation.

acceptance: Domain and architecture terms have one definition and no active contradictory aliases

actions.name: Arc42 - Glossary

states.description: Maintain all twelve arc42 sections as a coherent, traceable architecture whose deployment plan is derived from the documented environment.
states.name: Arc42

actions.description: Create Penpot wireframes for the architecturally approved flows using the current design contract and record stable design references for implementation.

acceptance: Penpot MCP is connected to an explicitly scoped file and page
Wireframes cover accepted flows, failure states, keyboard order and both accepted viewports
Repository evidence records stable Penpot object references without credentials

actions.name: Design - wireframes

actions.description: Derive reusable Penpot components and implementation mappings from the accepted wireframes without introducing a parallel token or component truth.

acceptance: Reusable components cover shared states and variants without duplicating DESIGN.md tokens
Component names and design references map unambiguously to intended implementation boundaries
Accessibility and responsive behavior are explicit

actions.name: Design - reusable components

states.description: Use Penpot to turn approved architecture and Ballet's design contract into implementable wireframes and reusable components.
states.name: Design

actions.description: Write the smallest requirement-linked tests first and prove that each new test fails only because the intended behavior is not implemented yet.

acceptance: Each new test names its requirement or quality scenario and the violated invariant
Targeted red evidence fails for the expected missing behavior rather than setup or unrelated regressions
No test is skipped, weakened or relabeled as passing

actions.name: Build - Write Tests (TDD)

actions.description: Implement the smallest architecture-conformant change that makes the targeted tests pass, then run all repository checks required by the affected boundaries.

acceptance: Targeted tests change from the recorded red state to green
Relevant success and failure paths pass without unrelated refactoring
All applicable repository checks are reported exactly

actions.name: Build - Write Code (Implement)

states.description: Use an explicit red-to-green TDD handoff to implement only the behavior authorized by the accepted architecture and design.
states.name: Build

actions.description: Deploy the verified build to the dev environment exactly as defined by the current arc42 Deployment View, without inferring a target or widening external-write authority.

acceptance: The deployment plan names an exact target, commands, version identity, health criteria and rollback
The external write has explicit action-scoped human authorization
The deployed version and immediate health evidence are recorded without secrets
deliverables: Dev deployment outcome with target, version and health evidence

actions.name: Deploy - Deploy to dev

actions.description: Run the acceptance scenarios defined by arc42 against the exact version deployed to dev and retain truthful pass, fail, blocked and pending evidence.

acceptance: Tests address the deployed version and environment from the preceding Action
Every in-scope quality scenario has an exact result or explicit blocker
No failing or unavailable external evidence is reported as passed
deliverables: Dev acceptance-test evidence and bounded handoff

actions.name: Deploy - Acceptance test

states.description: Follow the environment-specific arc42 deployment plan and prove the deployed dev build with acceptance evidence.
states.name: Deploy

actions.description: Explore the bounded domain as a chronological Big Picture and expose shared language, pivotal events, hotspots, actors, systems, values and open questions without inventing stakeholder knowledge.

acceptance: The timeline is chronological and names unresolved hotspots explicitly
The artifact links discoveries to existing project direction where evidence exists

actions.name: Event Storming - Big Picture Exploration

actions.description: Refine the Big Picture into bounded process flows with commands, actors, policies, read models, events, failure paths and measurable bottlenecks.

acceptance: Each modeled process traces commands through events and decision information
Failure paths, policies and unresolved domain questions remain visible

actions.name: Event Storming - Process Modeling

actions.description: Translate the approved process model into candidate aggregates, invariants, bounded contexts and technical boundaries while leaving architecture decisions for arc42 and human approval.

acceptance: Candidate boundaries trace to process evidence and name their invariants
Architecture-significant alternatives remain proposals rather than silently accepted decisions

actions.name: Event Storming - Software Design

states.description: Discover the problem space, model important processes and derive evidence-backed software design candidates before architecture documentation.
states.name: Event Storming
